children: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields extended declines on Friday as the yen strengthened on bets of faster Bank of Japan rate hikes and fading prospects of a U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate increase this month.
The 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 5.5 basis points (bps) to 2.91%. The 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) slipped 7  bps to 4.005%. Yields move inversely to bond prices.
"The selloff of JGBs and the yen has paused," said Katsutoshi Inadome, senior strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

There are various reasons for this, Inadome said. The one is expectations for the BOJ's hawkish stance, while dovish comments from Fed officials weakened bets for an early rate hike in the United States.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Thursday he would support keeping interest rates unchanged at the Fed's next policy meeting if upcoming data confirms inflation pressures are easing.
His comments followed remarks from New York Fed President John Williams, who said rising long-term bond yields reflected economic strength rather than inflation concerns.

The yen jumped by more than 2% against the U.S. dollar overnight. The gains were also supported by growing speculation that Japan's government pension fund (GPIF) is set to boost allocations to domestic bonds and yen-denominated assets following recent meetings.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has recently urged Japan to end its reflationary policies, which also helped reverse the trend of a weak yen and JGBs, said Inadome.

"Bessent's remarks may not be powerful enough to stop the selloff of JGBs in the long term, as his comments could affect Japan's monetary policy, but Japan's fiscal policy may not change," Inadome said.
